title: fix(permissions): keep session path grants that widen an existing rule
body:
Paired: [GitHub #10854](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/10854) ↔ [GitCode !9724](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/9724)

/kind bug

## Problem

In manual mode, "always allow for this session" on a path that already has a rule for another action is silently dropped, so the dialog reappears on the next call. Two independent defects produce the same symptom: the overlay key ignores the action axes, and compose appends one `file_guard.paths` entry per layer while the Engine keeps the first entry for an equal-length prefix.

Fixes #6271

## Change

- `permissions_layers`: overlays write per-axis increments against the layers below (Global and User for a Session overlay, Global and Session for a User overlay). A User overlay keeps its own rules that the increment does not mention, and a Session overlay only speaks through `allow`.
- `permission_compose`: `file_guard.paths` collapse to one entry per `(path, match)`, axes merged with the existing `_pick_level` precedence; intra-layer duplicates union with deny > allow > ask.
- Path identity: separators, trailing slashes and `~` are normalized for prefix rules only — glob paths stay verbatim because the Engine matches them literally. `match` collapses to the two values the Engine understands, and case folding applies only on Windows.
- A path axis no layer speaks about stays absent, so the Engine's own default decides (native `ask`, legacy `allow`). A User layer's `ask`, written as a filler when an approval grants a single axis, no longer tightens a lower `allow`.

## Behaviour changes worth reviewing

- A user-layer path `allow` now relaxes a global path `ask` for the same path. Previously the global entry won purely because it came first.
- Package builtin glob denies are appended after compose and are still resolved with "most severe wins", so `.ssh`, `.env` and key files stay denied.
- Residual limitation: `resolve()` is not applied, so `..`, symlinks, `$VAR` spellings and macOS case-insensitive volumes can still produce two entries that compile to one prefix.

## Tests

- New unit tests under `tests/unit_tests/agents/harness/`: a session overlay writes only the widened axis, identical axes are skipped, a User overlay never freezes a session-only axis, an existing user rule survives a permanent grant on another path, the real chain rebuilds to `ALLOW` without a prompt, same-path axes merge across layers, a durable deny survives a session allow, ordering and glob/prefix separation hold, and path identity normalizes as intended.
- `tests/unit_tests/agentserver/permissions` plus the three harness test files: 1980 passed, 0 failed.
- Known unrelated failure: `tests/agents/swarm/test_swarm_assembly.py` cannot be collected because it imports `jiuwenswarm.common.mode_matrix`, which an earlier commit removed.
